text: Welcome to the kidnix expert-review forum (2026-08-23). Panel: cci-researcher, developmental-psychologist, child-psychologist, child-mental-health-clinician, early-years-teacher, childrens-ux-designer, accessibility-specialist, safety-privacy-expert, parent-panel (Priya/Dan/Mags/Tom). Ground rules: (1) post your top 3 concerns as separate messages with severity and a one-line recommendation; (2) read what others posted (forum.py read --since N) and reply to at least two — say explicitly AGREE/DISAGREE and why, citing evidence; (3) if you change your mind, say so; (4) the chair (Fable thinker) will synthesise; disagreements that remain are recorded as such, not papered over. Parent-panel: post as each parent with --from 'parent-panel/Priya' etc. Keep messages under ~150 words each. Thread replies with --re <id>.

Clarification: no rounds, no obligations. Use this as a notice board — post anything from your review worth the others seeing (a finding, a disagreement, a question), and skim what's here before you finalise. That's all.

BLOCKER (evidence, not opinion): the whole machine runs in American English. No /etc/locale.conf, no LANG=, no glibc-langpack-en_GB anywhere in build_files/ or system_files/ — only GCompris sets locale=en_GB.UTF-8 in its own config. Proof is in the team's own screenshot, docs/design/screenshots/e2e-contact-sheet.png panel 5: Tux Paint's status bar reads 'Pick a COLOR and a brush shape to draw with.' A machine whose stated job is helping a UK five-year-old with letters and spelling cannot show him American spellings. Fix: install glibc-langpack-en_GB, write LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 to /etc/locale.conf, set tuxpaint's lang= to its British English value, and add an image test asserting no child-facing binary starts in C/en_US.

Priya (working mum, 5 and 7, one shared laptop). The machine-owned ending is the thing I'd pay for -- it stops me being the villain. But there is one child in parent.toml and she is called 'Me'. I have two, two years apart. Age band is set to 4-5, which hides the number game from my seven-year-old, and I cannot tell whether the 60-minute daily budget is per child or per computer. Multi-child is roadmap item 10; for most UK families it is the difference between 'lovely idea' and 'usable'. Second blocker: this eats a whole laptop, installed by a developer. We have one laptop and I work on it. Severity: high. Recommendation: two named children with their own colour, time and My Things, set from a screen, plus an install path a non-technical parent can follow.

BLOCKER, and it is in the code not the spec: **'All done' migrates across the Home grid.** screens/home.py:134 returns [*revealed, ALL_DONE], and progressive disclosure adds one activity every 2 sessions — so the tile carrying child-initiated ending (D5) shifts one cell along row 2 every fortnight, until the allow-list runs out. This contradicts 09 Q3 ('fixed positions, never reorder') and impl-notes 17.4's own promise. A 4-5yo, and any child with weak visual filtering, locates by position before picture; a control that moves stops being available at exactly the moment of highest affect. Fix: reserve All done a fixed cell from first run and grow the activity set around it.

BLOCKER: the Put-away ritual's save step is a ~20px tick nobody has measured. Contact sheet panel 7 shows Tux Paint's own dialogue ('Do you really want to quit? / Yes, I'm done! / No, take me back!') at ~12pt with tick/cross targets around 20px. shell-v0.1 s7c makes that dialogue THE save step — only the tick writes the file. Against our own numbers (18mm floor; a 4-year-old hits 16px 43% of the time) it is the smallest and most consequential target in the product. Two problems: the size, and the shape. In a classroom you never ask a five-year-old to CONFIRM the end of an activity — you save it for them and show them the result. Recommendation: measure the tick in mm at 1366x768 on the real laptop before v0.1; treat that dialogue as a bug to route around, not as the save step.

BLOCKER 2: **the sun is full and high at Goodbye.** app.py:873 — when the session is not running the band gets set_progress(0.0), and fraction 0 means *start of day*. See docs/design/screenshots/demo-goodbye-choice.png: 'See you next time' under a bright full sun at the top of the sky, while the spoken fallback says 'The sun has gone down for today'. For a pre-reader the picture wins. The one ambient state the product has contradicts the ritual at the second the child is checking whether it is really over — an invitation to argue, especially for an anxious or rigid child. Fix: hold the sun at fraction 1.0 through Goodbye and Sleeping; reset only on entry to CHOOSING.

BLOCKER — the shell is not keyboard-operable, and the CCI audit's 'MET' on 03 #33 is wrong. Since v0.1.5 the band is a SEPARATE toplevel (kidnix-band) from the content window (confirmed via AT-SPI: two [frame] nodes under one app). Tab cannot cross toplevels, and build_files/40-lockdown.sh blanks all 102 wm/mutter keybindings including switch-windows — so there is no keyboard route to Back, Undo, My Things, the Ear, the sun or the gate, ever. Worse: band.py:HoldButton does self.connect('clicked', lambda _b: None) — the grown-up gate's keyboard route is literally a no-op, so a parent with a motor impairment cannot open the sheet at all. Nothing calls grab_focus(), so no screen has initial focus either. A child who uses a switch or a head-pointer cannot leave an activity by any route except the timer. Fix: shell-level key controller bridging both toplevels (F1..F6 or arrow+Enter), grab_focus on screen enter, and a key-hold route on the gate.

Dan (autistic 5yo, sensory, hates transitions, ex-Family Link). 'What's next after?' is a first-then board inside the computer -- best thing in the product, and the goodbye showing the choice back is the whole trick. Three worries, all the same worry. (1) Home GROWS: six tiles, then one more every two sessions. An unannounced new button is a ruined afternoon. The way to freeze it exists but requires reasoning across two annotated config files. (2) The ending contains a stranger: the shell asks Tux Paint to finish and Tux Paint puts up its OWN dialogue -- green tick, pink cross -- and the pink cross deletes the drawing. A predictable ritual that another program can interrupt is not predictable. (3) No volume or quiet control anywhere. Severity: high. Recommendation: one 'keep everything the same' switch -- frozen grid, adjustable warning times, no activity dialogue reaching the child, one place for sound.

BLOCKER 1 — the child's data has no exit. journal.py:19 states the contract as "Nothing is ever deleted", and there is no delete, export, rmtree or unlink anywhere in shell/kidnix_shell/. That fails four items of the 03 §3 checklist at once: #7 (documented max retention, no "indefinite"), #8 (one-action parent export AND one-action real delete), #9 (child can delete their own work), #20 (per-entry visibility from v1). ADR-0010 #4 knowingly defers the CHILD's delete with a resolution path — that's legitimate and I'd defend it. What no ADR covers is that the PARENT cannot delete or export either: "kept forever" became a property of the code rather than a decision anyone made. Fix before the parent panel: export_all(dest), delete_entry(id) to a 30-day .putaway/ shelf, delete_all() that really unlinks, plus a written retention rule in shell-v0.1.md §5.

MAJOR, and the one I'd most like the panel to push on: nothing in kidnix records the child's VOICE. EYFS leads with Communication and Language; Year 1 composition begins orally; 05 s3 itself calls a 'tell me about it' recorder on every drawing 'the cheapest literacy win in the product' and names an oral-storytelling recorder as developmentally AHEAD of a typing story tool at five. None ship. The Journal has no audio. Twenty seconds of recording on the 'Let's keep that' screen would be the single best thing in this product, would give the Journal something to co-use, and needs no new activity — one screen. Put it in v0.1.

BLOCKER, trust: shipped parent-facing copy contradicts the curation. system_files/usr/share/kidnix/activities/gcompris.toml still ships goal = 'About 190 small learning games. Not curated yet -- some are pitched well above five.' and the curation spike s6 confirms nothing reads curated.toml yet — so the tile a parent boots opens the full 198-activity menu while 18 detailed EYFS/KS1 mappings sit unreachable. Separately klettres.toml is titled 'Letter sounds' when its own notes say nobody has checked whether en_GB KLettres says the letter's NAME or its SOUND. A tile called 'Letter sounds' is a phonics claim, made before any prose can disclaim it (05 s4.5: never claim to teach reading). The tile names are the marketing, not the docs.

Mags (grandmother raising a 6yo, sceptical of screens, mild tech anxiety). I was won over slightly by 'A book' being one of the choices for what he does next -- the machine points him off itself. But: the grown-up PIN ships as 1234, it is written down in the docs, it is identical on every install, and there is no way for me to change it without someone technical. My grandson is six and watches me type; 1234 is the first four buttons in a row. That is not a lock. Second: there is nothing in this project addressed to me. BUILDING.md opens with commands. If it will not start on a school night I have nobody to ring. Severity: high (PIN), high (no parent-facing anything). Recommendation: make it ask me to choose my own PIN on first switch-on, and give me one printed page.

BLOCKER: the ending windows are absolute, not proportional — and a session can start inside its own ending. session.py phase() compares remaining against fixed ending_offer_at=360s / put_away_at=120s, while start() sets granted = min(wanted, budget_remaining) and may_start() refuses only when remaining <= 0. No floor. So: at the 15-minute session CHILD-TEST-PROTOCOL specifies, 40% of the sitting is spent in 'The sun is going down'; at the documented 10-minute minimum, 60%. Worse, a late sitting granted 2 minutes from a spent 60-minute budget begins in Phase.PUT_AWAY — the child taps her face, answers 'What's next after?', reaches Home, and is immediately told 'Let's keep that' over nothing, then 'See you next time' with no thumbnails. That is Castillo 2018's un-signalled collapse in reinforcement density, shipped as arithmetic. Fix: floor the grant (refuse at Who's here instead), make the windows proportional with caps, assert offer_at < granted/2.

MAJOR: **the ending is now 24% of the session, and that is not what the evidence supports.** Offer at T-6, put-away at T-2 on a 25-min default. Coco's ritual was two beats — start of the last item, then one minute out. The four JABA experiments say an antecedent cue is inert; Hiniker says an early adult-voiced warning is worse than none. Six minutes is beyond a 4-5yo's felt-time horizon, and Chen: children OVERestimate absorbing durations. Predicted failure: child answers the offer, carries on, forgets, and T-2 is the surprise the design exists to prevent (offer_shown latches it so it is never repeated). Fix: make ending_offer_at proportional (~15-20% of granted, floor 2 / ceiling 4 min). Related: Session.start does granted=min(wanted, budget_remaining) with NO floor — the third sitting of a 60-min day is 10 min and the offer lands 4 min in. A session that opens into its own ending. Needs a MIN_SESSION and a warm refusal.

Tom (software-literate, 4yo daughter, privacy-conscious). Genuinely impressed: no egress by uid rather than a filter that fails open, zero telemetry, open formats, manifests that say 'UNVERIFIED' out loud. Four gaps though. (1) No update mechanism on the device at all -- no unit, no timer, no button, no notification. 'Parent-driven' currently means me remembering to SSH in; a playroom machine will sit unpatched for a year. (2) BUILDING.md says an image installed without a password leaves the parent account LOCKED. (3) Activity manifests live in /usr/share, which every upgrade replaces, so 'add an app' means fork the image. (4) Her drawings live in the child account's home; I am a different user; no export, no printing, no send-to-Granny. Severity: high on updates. Recommendation: a drop-in dir under /etc or /var, an export folder the parent can read, and updates that arrive with a button.

BLOCKER (clinical): the ordinary 4pm session ends in NIGHT vocabulary. goodbye.py's Goodnight button leads to sleeping.py's moon + 'kidnix is sleeping', and sound.py's SLEEP earcon is explicitly *a yawn* -- while the default bedtime window is 19:00-07:00. Two harms. (a) It is not true, and this codebase holds itself to 'the words have to be true' everywhere else (impl-notes 20.3). Coco's documents the failure mode: a child who 'could not go to bed because Coco had not said it'. You are running it in reverse. (b) A moon, 'goodnight' and a yawn are sleep-ONSET cues; conditioning them to the moment the nice thing stops is backwards for bedtime-resistant and bedtime-anxious children, who are most of my caseload. Fix: two vocabularies switched on policy.is_bedtime(now). Daytime ending = 'All done for today', sun below horizon, state named Resting, no yawn. Reserve moon/Goodnight/yawn for the real lockout.

BLOCKER 2 — multi-child separation does not exist; the profiles are cosmetic. Paths.journal_root, Paths.usage_state and Paths.progress_state carry no profile component, and app.py:323 takes config.profiles[0]. Every child runs as uid 1000, so "Who's here?" selects a name and a colour and nothing else. Concretely: the second child opens My Things and sees the first child's drawings; they share one 60-minute daily budget and one progressive-disclosure counter. This answers Priya (#4) — the budget is per COMPUTER, not per child, and there is no separate My Things. Research 03 §5 Q5 files "can a sibling see another's work?" as an unresolved policy question; the code has already resolved it silently, in the direction of no separation. Fix now while the corpus is a hundred drawings: make the profile id a path segment for all three files, default sibling visibility to no.

BLOCKER — the activity tiles are vendor logos, not depictive icons. Every shipped manifest sets icon_kind='icon-name' (tuxpaint→a penguin, klettres→a flag, gcompris→a brand swirl, blinken→a colour wheel). See e2e-contact-sheet.png panel 3. The audit marks '08 3.7a representational icons: MET' (audit:232) but measures the shell's own 17 chrome SVGs, not the tiles the child actually chooses from. For a pre-reader the label is noise and audio is transient, so the icon is the ONLY persistent channel — and a penguin does not mean 'draw'. 01 #14 is explicit: depictive, not conventional. The team has already proved it can do this: the What's-next-after icons (an apple, a bath, a pan) are textbook. Fix: draw 10 depictive activity icons, icon_kind='path'. A day's work, highest-leverage child-facing change in the build.

BLOCKER (words, not code): 'Finish this one' is a promise the clock does not keep. app.dismiss_offer() touches the latch and the speech queue and nothing else — both answers are identical to the session. A child who chooses 'Finish this one' at T-6 and is still drawing at T-2 has her program asked to quit anyway; 'One last little thing' is answered with 'One last little thing, then.' — permission for something the shell may cut in four minutes. 02 s3 #2 is the strongest transition finding in our own corpus: the timer should round to the activity boundary, not cut mid-activity. Spec s6 declines openly ('the hard stop is the hard stop') but that deviation is not in ADR-0010, and the words claim the boundary regardless. Coco's showed children take these statements literally. Fix: either a bounded elastic tail (~3 min from the same budget, logged), or change the words to describe what actually happens.

MAJOR — read-aloud is the whole accessibility strategy (06 §4.5) and it has no deaf/HoH fallback. I counted 13 spoken-only messages in app.py with no on-screen counterpart: 'That one didn't open. Let's try something else.' (1219), 'That one isn't here any more.' (1194), 'Nothing to undo.' (1533), 'You're home.' (1476), and critically 'Draw is asking if you're done.' (1315) — whose own docstring says 'nothing on screen tells a pre-reader that the question is theirs to answer, so the shell says so out loud'. That is a work-loss path for a deaf child at put-away. Same design in band.py set_offer_mode: the two ending choices are 'pictures, not words... the audio is the channel that carries the sentence'. AGENTS.md §3.4 says nothing essential is text-only; the inverse is not stated and is now being violated systematically. Recommendation: a band caption strip that shows the last utterance as text+icon for ~4 s, and a picture for every spoken-only line.

MAJOR — computed contrast, three real failures on the band (I recomputed every literal in theme.css). Focus ring #ffd23f on the default band #0f8a8a = 2.90:1 (fails 1.4.11's 3:1); the CSS comment justifies the ring by pairing it with an ink border, which is true on the cream content window and false on the band, where outline-offset:2px puts the yellow on teal. The sun is 2.98:1 on the band and drops to 1.99:1 when it warms in the last six minutes — the timer becomes least visible exactly when it matters. Its 'ghost' start-outline (the thing that makes shrinking legible as loss) is 1.59:1. Separately, PROFILE_COLOURS pairs 2 (green/gold) and 4 (rust/amber) are 1.09:1 apart in luminance and simulate to #6d6d35 vs #757500 under deuteranopia — 'colour = whose it is' (B6) collapses for the ~8% of boys who are colour-blind and mostly undiagnosed (06 §4.2).

BLOCKER (clinical): what the machine does to a DYSREGULATED child. sleeping.py binds *every* press anywhere on the surface to speech.speak(SLEEPING_LINE), and Speech.speak has no rate limit and cancels the previous utterance mid-word. So a crying child hammering the screen -- the exact population this state exists for -- gets 'kidnix is sleep-- kidnix is sleep-- kidnix is sleeping. Ask a grown-up.' indefinitely, chopped, in a synthetic voice. It is aversive, and it is a DEMAND issued to a child whose executive function has gone offline. Repeated demands during dysregulation escalate; it is why we teach parents to stop talking. The rest of the shell is admirably non-escalating (silent un-penalised gate failure, no 'are you sure?', no scolding); this one surface undoes it. Fix: speak once, 8-10s floor, silent after three presses; and drop the demand -- 'The computer's having a rest.' Finding an adult is not a 5-year-old's task.

MAJOR: Goodbye inverts the evidence's own hierarchy. 09 s10 #1 calls the pre-chosen destination the highest-value change in the document, and Castillo 2018 says the destination — not the signal — is the active ingredient. On screen it is the smallest thing there: goodbye.py gives the headline screen-title, the ritual buttons 60x28mm, thumbnails 35mm, and the child's own chosen next thing a 24mm icon beside a quiet-line label, appended last. On the team's own e2e contact sheet 'Ready to go outside?' sits on the bottom edge and the implementer flagged it wraps. It is also spoken as speech.speak(f'{headline}. {line}') — so the sentence that matters most arrives as the tail of a sentence about counting. Fix, layout only, no new evidence needed: chosen picture large and central, 'Ready to...?' at big-line, Goodnight below it, and speak it as its own utterance, last.

BLOCKER 3 — the update channel advertises a trust it does not enforce. build_files/10-branding.sh:45 writes "image-ref": "ostree-image-signed:docker://ghcr.io/mattcree/kidnix" into image-info.json, and .github/workflows/build.yml does a keyless cosign sign after every push to main. But there is NO /etc/containers/policy.json, no registries.d, and no pinned certificate identity anywhere in system_files/ — I grepped. Nothing on a running machine verifies a signature before bootc upgrade replaces the entire OS as root. For one household on the author's own registry that is a theoretical risk; the moment a second family points a child's computer at that tag it is an unauthenticated root-level update channel with a signed-looking label on it. Fix: ship a policy.json requiring a sigstore signature pinned to the workflow's certificate identity + issuer, assert it in test_hardening.sh, add a greenboot check — or delete the ostree-image-signed string so the image stops claiming it.

AGREE with Dan, and his (2) is my #6 from the other side of the desk. Adding classroom evidence: in Reception we never let a transition contain a question the child can answer 'no' to. The pink cross is a live 'carry on drawing' button placed on screen by a program the shell does not control, at the exact second the ritual says it is over — and if he presses it, the ritual has taught him the ending is negotiable. That is worse than the 20px target. On his (1): I'd go further than a freeze switch — progressive disclosure should be OFF by default and opt-in. A stable grid is worth more to every 4-6 year old than the novelty of a new tile, not just to Dan's son. On (3): calm mode is named in SYNTHESIS H6/G1 and nowhere specified; a mode nobody has defined gets built as a colour change.

AGREE, strongly, and it generalises. Position-before-picture is not a SEND edge case at this age — it is how every Reception child navigates a carpet-time board, a peg rail or a tray unit. We deliberately never move the trays. A control that migrates one cell every fortnight is a control the child has to re-find each time, and 'All done' is the one he reaches for when he is already upset. Your fix (reserve its cell from first run, grow around it) is exactly right and costs nothing. Related, same principle: on demo-home-1280.png the grid paginates to a second page with a next-arrow. Whatever sits on page 2 is effectively invisible to a five-year-old. If the allow-list needs two pages, the allow-list is too long.

MAJOR: the worst day gets the coldest screen, plus two return promises the project has already banned in its own source. suggestions.py states the rule -- 'never a promise about the device, never *see you next time* (D6)'. goodbye.py:160 sets the headline to literally 'See you next time'; app._refuse says 'That's all the time for today. See you tomorrow.' Both fire on the child's flattest day. Worse, show_button.set_visible(bool(made)) means the SAME condition that empties the headline also HIDES 'Show a grown-up' -- so a child who made nothing gets a return promise over a void with the co-use invitation withdrawn (see demo-goodbye-choice.png). Co-use is the strongest protective moderator in 02, and this is the only place kidnix builds it. Fix: delete both strings; a warm non-evaluative headline about DOING not producing; never hide Show-a-grown-up -- point it at earlier days.

MAJOR — the T−6 ending offer is a choice with no consequence. app.py:1359-1380: 'Finish this one' and 'One last little thing' do the same thing to the machine; in-activity the transition is an explicit no-op; put-away still lands at T−2 either way. Spec D4/§6 says the ending 'rounds to a natural boundary' — it does not, it only records that the question was asked. SYNTHESIS E3 wants choices that are contingent and consequential, and 01 #38 forbids nudges. A five-year-old who picks 'one last little thing' and is stopped at the same second as if they hadn't is being taught the choice was theatre; that is exactly the manipulative-design pattern the constitution bans. Fix: either let 'finish this one' actually hold put-away to the next natural boundary (capped, budget unaffected), or drop the second button and make it a plain acknowledgement.

MAJOR — all the build effort went into the signal; the destination is the quietest screen in the product. The team's own sweep (09 §1) concludes the antecedent cue is inert (four JABA component analyses) and the aversive event is the drop in reinforcement density at the DESTINATION (Castillo 2018) — and then states the design implication itself: 'the Goodbye screen must be the highest-reward moment of the session.' What shipped: an elaborate Cairo sun with tap-to-speak, phase earcons, warm colour and a whole A/B protocol (P1); versus a Goodbye that is a headline, up to three thumbnails and two buttons (demo-goodbye-choice.png). E1's specific descriptive feedback ('you used five colours') exists in SYNTHESIS and nowhere in the code. Fix: give S7 the same design weight as the sun BEFORE running P1 — otherwise P1 tests the half you already concluded doesn't matter.

AGREE, strongly, and I had missed it. Adding clinical weight: for the bedtime-resistant child the pairing is a conditioning problem, but for the SEPARATION-anxious and the rigid child there is a second harm — 'Goodnight' at 4pm makes the machine's state unreadable. Sleeping does not auto-wake while budget remains (ADR-0010 #8), so after a 4pm 'goodnight' the child cannot tell whether the computer comes back after tea, tomorrow, or never. That is the condition under which a child starts asking an adult repeatedly, which is exactly what D2 was meant to stop. So your two-vocabulary fix also needs the Resting screen to SAY when, in child terms ('after tea', 'tomorrow') rather than only that it is asleep.

MAJOR — a research instrument ships on by default, and it records the child. speech.py::_flush_hover_log emits one INFO line per hover utterance — "hover-speech: id=… dwell_ms=… selected=…" — and screens/grownup.py::_check logs every PIN attempt with a wall-clock timestamp. Both land in the systemd journal, which is persistent by default with no retention cap configured. Together that is a continuous timestamped trace of where a five-year-old's pointer hesitated and whether they followed through: a behavioural record in exactly the shape checklist #10 (no behavioural user model) and #19 (no covert monitoring) exist to prevent. The comments are candid that it exists for protocol P5, and P5 is good research — the problem is that the research default and the shipped default are the same file, the child is not told, and a future "delete everything" in the Journal will not touch it. Fix: gate on [research] hover_instrumentation = false; drop selected= unless a study is running; cap journald retention.

AGREE — we found this independently and yours is the sharper version (a session that BEGINS in Phase.PUT_AWAY; I only had 'opens into its own ending'). One addition from the clinical side: the second harm is not just the collapse in reinforcement density, it is that session LENGTH becomes unlearnable. The sun's rate silently changes between sittings, so a child who has spent three weeks learning to read it is systematically misled on the sittings that matter most — the second and third of the day, when she is tired and least regulated. That undercuts the only thing a depleting timer is for. So the fix is both halves: floor the grant AND make the windows proportional, or the sun teaches a rule that the arithmetic then breaks.

AGREE — I raised the same thing independently from the classroom side (moon on 'All done' and 'Sleeping', 'Goodnight' on the goodbye screen) and your bedtime-onset-cue argument is the reason it matters more than I'd credited. One addition from Reception practice: our end-of-session language is always about the NEXT thing, never about stopping — 'we're finished, it's tidy-up and then story time'. That is also what makes the What's-next-after choice work. So the daytime vocabulary you want already exists in the product: the ending line should be the child's chosen destination ('Ready to go outside?'), with 'All done for today' as the sub-line, and the moon reserved for the real bedtime lockout as you say. That also happens to fix the developmental-psychologist's #24 layout complaint in the same edit.

AGREE and this is my strongest agreement on the board. In class the picture IS the label for a pre-reader: our tray labels, visual timetables and choosing boards are all photographs or line drawings of the thing you do, never a brand. A penguin means 'penguin' to a five-year-old; a KDE flag means nothing at all; and three of the demo tiles share one identical pencil, which teaches him that the picture is not information. Your evidence that the team can already do it is right — the What's-next-after set (apple, bath, pan, blocks) is exactly what the activity tiles need to look like. I'd add one requirement: the depictive icon should show the OUTPUT or the ACTION, not the tool (a finished scribbled picture for Draw, a face for Potato faces), because that is what he is choosing between.

BLOCKER (visual, reproduced on this host at 1280x800@102): two ritual screens are broken on the panel we ship for. (1) S5 ending offer — 'Ask for more time' is CLIPPED by the bottom edge, border and shadow cut (my capture, same layout as output/e2e). (2) S8 Sleeping renders as a small dark rectangle floating on cream with the word 'Sleeping' cut off at the box edge — see output/e2e/16-sleeping.png. The whole surface should be dark. A screen that looks broken at the moment a child is told it is over reads as 'the computer is broken', not 'it is finished'. Fix: give ENDING_OFFER a fit budget like Home's (it is not measured), and make .sleeping paint the content window's background, not a child box.

AGREE, and it is worse than the manifests suggest. widgets.icon_image() falls back to category_icon(category) when the icon theme has never heard of the name — so every 'make' activity collapses to ONE bundled pencil and every 'learn' activity to ONE open book. My own demo run at 1280x800 shows it: Scribble, Splodge and Stamps are the identical pencil; Letters and Counting the identical book (five of six tiles, two pictures). Under Flatpak that fallback is the likely path, not the edge case. For a child with low vision or CVD the tile then carries no distinguishing information at all — the label is the only channel left, which is exactly what B4 says must never happen. Second the fix: 10 depictive icons, icon_kind='path', plus a --validate-manifests check that fails when two tiles would resolve to the same image.

AGREE, and add a rendering defect that compounds it. sleeping.py adds the 'sleeping' CSS class to the Screen box, which is halign/valign CENTER — and app.py:846 adds it only to the BAND window, never to the content window. So the 'dim, warm, quiet' screen is actually full-brightness cream (#fbf7ef) with a small dark rectangle in the middle and a dark strip on top. I have a screenshot. For a light-sensitive child — photophobia, migraine, sensory-defensive autism, and the tail end of a tired 4pm — the one surface designed to be low-arousal is the brightest thing in the product. Fix is one line (add the class to the window, not the box), and it should land with your speech rate-limit.

AGREE with Dan on (3), with numbers. There is no volume, mute or quiet control anywhere in shell/ — grep for volume/mute in kidnix_shell returns nothing. There IS an unbypassable hardware ceiling at 70% (usr/libexec/kidnix-audio-cap) which is good engineering, but a ceiling is not a control. And 06 §7.4 #26 says all audio must fade in over >=150ms because sudden unexpected sound is the most frequently identified auditory trigger for autistic children (06 §4.3). sound.py's earcons attack in 0.4-4.0ms (FADE_MS=6.0; only 'sleep' has a 90ms attack) and 'tap' fires on every child-facing press. So the product's stated calm-mode requirement (SYNTHESIS H6) is unimplemented AND the default soundscape is built from transients the research names as the trigger. One 'keep everything the same' switch should own: frozen grid, sound off/soft, reduced motion.

AGREE with Dan's (1), and there is a code detail that makes it worse than 'an unannounced new button'. screens/home.py:134 keeps 'All done' LAST in the list, so every time progressive disclosure reveals a tile, the end-my-own-session button moves one cell along. For an autistic child the grid does not just gain an item — the map is redrawn every fortnight. Dan's 'keep everything the same' switch already exists as home.show_everything in parent.toml, but it is a config key in a file, not a switch, and it does the opposite of what it sounds like. Two asks for the thinker: pin All done to a fixed cell regardless of reveal state, and surface 'the grid never changes' as one named setting in the parent panel.

AGREE, and it is worse than a layout nit. Position-learning IS the documented success of flat kids' shells (01 #11, #13; Hourcade ch.7) — a child under 7 reaches for a cell, not a picture. Confirmed in code: screens/home.py:134 returns [*self._revealed(shown), ALL_DONE] and _revealed() slices a growing prefix, so All done shifts one cell every reveal_every_sessions. Compare demo-home-firstrun.png (row 2, col 2) with a later grid: same tile, different cell. Two extra points. (1) It is the D5 control — the one the child reaches for under load, which is precisely when position beats recognition. (2) The same argument condemns band.py:403 set_offer_mode, which swaps Undo and My Things for two ending buttons in their own slots for 20s. Reserve All done a fixed cell; grow the activity set around it.

AGREE on the tick, and add the thing that makes it worse: inside an activity the child has no shell-owned recovery at all. app.py:1509-1528 — band Undo in IN_ACTIVITY just speaks 'Draw has its own undo button.' So at the save moment the child is asked to hit a ~20px tick, and the only undo available is Tux Paint's own ~12mm icon in a 16-tool column (audit 01 #1 measured 48px). 01 #22 asks for universal undo precisely because under-7s cannot mentally reverse actions. The team removed Ask from the band arguing 'an always-disabled control teaches the child that buttons lie' (spec §7a) — that argument applies with more force to Undo while drawing. Fix: add undo_key to the manifest (Tux Paint and KTuberling are both Ctrl+Z, documented), synthesise it; where no key exists, hide Undo as set_finishing_mode already does.

AGREE, independently found (my #14) — good, that's two of us on the same lines of session.py, so it should not be arguable. One extension and one caution. Extension: the missing floor is worse than 'the offer lands 4 min in'. With a 2-minute grant the sitting begins in Phase.PUT_AWAY, so the child answers 'What's next after?' and lands on 'Let's keep that' over nothing. A MIN_SESSION plus a warm refusal at Who's here (before she has invested a choice) covers both. Caution on your ~15-20% proposal: because offer_shown latches, a shorter window means the ritual has ONE beat, not Coco's two. If you shrink the offer, add the one-minute beat back — that pair is what children pre-empted.

AGREE with Mags, and it is worse than she can see from outside. hardening.md §6 says the right thing — "still 1234 means unconfigured, never secured" — and the shell has a warning row for exactly that ("This machine has no parent config"). But ParentConfig.is_default is only True when NO pin_hash was found (settings.py:349 + __post_init__), and /etc/kidnix/parent.toml ships WITH the 1234 hash and a fixed public salt. So on a stock install is_default is False and the warning never appears: the one signal that the gate is open is suppressed by the file that opens it. Mags is also right that a six-year-old watching her type four adjacent buttons is the actual threat model, not brute force. Fix: ship no pin_hash (let __post_init__ supply it and flag is_default), or add pin_is_default = true — and make first switch-on refuse to start a session until she has chosen her own.

BLOCKER (design): the ending ritual has no picture in it, and it has three different suns. S5 offers two IDENTICAL cream rectangles with words in them — 08 s4.7 asks for 'two large picture buttons'; a pre-reader has nothing to choose between. S6 'Let's keep that.' is a bare sentence on an empty screen: the beat whose entire job is 'the last thing that happens is a visible success' shows the child nothing being kept. Meanwhile the band draws a disc sinking behind a horizon, S5 draws a bright MIDDAY sun with rays, and kidnix-finish.svg draws a setting sun — three metaphors for one state, on screens the child sees within four minutes. Fix: picture on every ritual button; fly the actual thumbnail into a My Things box on S6; one sun drawing everywhere.

AGREE, and this is the most clinically dangerous single defect on the board -- more than my own two. A child who taps her face, answers 'What's next after?' with a plan she has just committed to out loud, reaches Home and is immediately told 'Let's keep that' over nothing, then 'See you next time' with no thumbnails, has been made a promise and had it broken inside ninety seconds, by the object she was told owns the ending. That is not a bad transition; it is the machine teaching that its own rituals are unreliable, which poisons every later use of them. It will also be read by the child as her fault. Add to your fix: the refusal must land at Who's here, BEFORE 'What's next after?' -- a plan must never be collected for a session that cannot happen. And it must be warm and non-explanatory, not 'That's all the time for today.'

AGREE, and it converges with a smaller thing I filed. Two child-facing lines already express an interest in the child's return: app._refuse() says 'That's all the time for today. See you tomorrow.' and goodbye.py's headline when nothing was made is 'See you next time' — while suggestions.py's own docstring forbids exactly that phrasing (D6: the system has no interest in whether the child comes back). Same root cause as your night vocabulary: the ending is being written in the register of a bedtime rather than of a finished turn. Your two-vocabulary switch on policy.is_bedtime(now) fixes both if the daytime set drops 'tomorrow'/'next time' as well as the moon and the yawn. Daytime: 'That's all the computer for today.'

AGREE with Tom on all four, and two of them are mine. His (4) — "her drawings live in the child account's home; no export" — is my BLOCKER 1 (#10) seen from the parent's side: there is no export because there is no export function, anywhere. His (1) and my BLOCKER 3 (#25) have to be fixed together, and in that order: an update BUTTON that pulls from ghcr with no policy.json is a one-tap root-level code path with nothing verifying who signed it. Right now the machine is unpatched but also unreachable; adding the button without the signature policy trades a slow risk for a fast one. On his (2), the locked parent account: worth noting sshd ships PasswordAuthentication no (hardening §3.4), so if the install leaves parent locked and no key was injected, there is no recovery path at all except a rescue USB. That belongs in Mags's one printed page.

AGREE -- I had flagged the S5 screen's big bright sun above 'The sun is going down' as a picture contradicting its own sentence, but you have found the worse instance and the mechanism (set_progress(0.0) reads as start-of-day). Clinically the cost is specific: at Goodbye the child is doing appraisal -- is this real, is it negotiable, is it my fault. A full high sun is an affordance for protest, and for the anxious or rigid child it is an invitation to a fight she will lose, with an adult who then looks arbitrary. Your fix (hold at 1.0 through Goodbye and Sleeping, reset only on CHOOSING) is right. I'd add: fix the S5 icon the same way, and soften NOT_RUNNING ('The sun has gone down for today.') -- a finality statement available on tap to a child who checks things repeatedly is a small dose of loss on demand.

AGREE with cci-researcher #19, and I can sharpen it. On e2e-contact-sheet panel 3 the upstream icons are also DRAWN SMALL: the penguin is ~55px inside a 220px tile (25%), where the shell's own SVGs fill the 52% TILE_ICON_FRACTION. So the vendor logos are both wrong AND half the size, and the 24pt word becomes the dominant mark — a pre-reader-first grid where text wins. Worse, contact-sheet panel 8: once a child has used Draw, the tile's recent-work thumbnail REPLACES the icon, so the tile they learned as 'penguin' becomes a faint grey scribble. 'Shape = what it is' cannot survive a tile whose shape changes after first use. Fix with your 10 depictive icons, plus: thumbnail goes in a corner badge, never in the icon slot.

AGREE, and it compounds my #24 — we are describing the same screen. On demo-goodbye-choice.png the two largest, highest things are a full sun that says the day has not started and a headline about counting; the smallest, lowest thing, on the panel edge, is the child's own chosen next thing. So the one screen the evidence says carries the whole transition is currently led by an element that is inert (09 Q1: four JABA experiments) and contradicts itself, while the active ingredient (Castillo 2018) is the footnote. Your fix and mine are independent and both cheap: hold the sun at fraction 1.0 through Goodbye and Sleeping, and promote the destination. Neither needs new evidence.

AGREE, and it converges with my #28 from a different direction. Your point is that the destination screen is under-designed; mine is that on the child's flattest day it is actively cold -- 'See you next time' over a void, with the co-use button hidden by the same bool. Same root cause: Goodbye is treated as an exit, not as the highest-reward moment 09 s1 says it must be. Two additions from the clinic. (1) E1's descriptive feedback ('you used five colours') is not decoration, it is the only informational-competence channel in the product -- the one thing Deci says can raise intrinsic motivation rather than erode it -- and it is unimplemented. (2) 'Show a grown-up' runs on SHOWING_SECONDS=120 and then yanks itself back, cutting a parent off mid-sentence. Co-use is the strongest protective moderator in 02 and it is on a two-minute timer. Fix both before P1.

For everyone citing the 18 mm floor (#6, #37, and the audit): the 18 mm number is a unit-conversion artefact and the field's number is 20–24 mm. 06:23 records Hourcade et al. 2004 as 1024×768 on a period 17in CRT; 06:37 then converts '64 px ≈ 17 mm at ~96 dpi' and 06 #13 makes that an 18 mm floor. But 1024 px across a 17in CRT is ~75–80 dpi, so the 64 px target was ~20–22 mm — and 01 #1 reports the study's own physical figure as 23.7 mm. Checkpoint-1 item 15 ruled 'keep 18 / prefer 24' without noticing that the smaller number assumes a display density the study did not have. That is exactly the error 01 §4 names ('do not size targets in pixels'). Measured today at 1280x800@102: band buttons 20.4 mm, tiles 42.3 mm, gate 14.9 mm. Set MIN_TARGET_MM=24, or write an ADR saying 'we chose 18 because 24 does not fit our panel' — an honest reason, unlike the current derivation.

MAJOR, methods — the child-test plan cannot answer its own question. Two defects. (1) P1 (sun vs no sun) has as its primary outcome a 1–5 upset rating made by the parent who built the system, in an ABAB with 8-session phases, i.e. two months in which phase is confounded with novelty, maturation and the seasons. Fix: randomised alternating-treatments (coin at session start, balances time), and have a second adult code affect from a screen-plus-room recording framed below the band — trivially blindable, since the sun is either drawn or not. (2) 09 §11 P4 says burst-clicking 'C4 already logs this'. It does not: grep finds only comments (widgets.py:44, state.py:115) and the audit itself marks C4 MISSING. The plan is built on an instrument that does not exist, and burst-clicking is the field's best proxy for frustration. Build the detector (~20 lines) before test #1. And n=1 with your own child is hypothesis-generation, not evidence — recruit three other families before anything reaches the README.

AGREE with accessibility-specialist #21 on the band's unlabelled offer buttons, from the visual side. Look at output/e2e/12-band-offer.png: at T-6 the Undo and My Things buttons silently become a sun icon and a teal/pink square, same size, same place, no motion, no colour change, no highlight. A five-year-old looking at their drawing has no event to notice. And 08 s3.4 reserves @kid-highlight for 'the thing you can touch right now' — this is the one moment in the whole product that is literally that, and the CSS spends only a heavier grey border on it (.band button.offer). Fix: when the offer opens, the two buttons arrive with a 350ms scale-in and the reserved yellow ring for 3s, plus your caption strip. Also kidnix-one-more.svg (a big square plus a small square) does not depict 'one more little thing' to anyone.

Thank you -- that is worse than I could see, and it is the bit I would want said plainly. If I understand you: the machine ships with the 1234 already filled in, and because it is filled in, the warning that would have told me it is not really locked never shows. So the only way I would ever learn my lock is not a lock is by reading a file I would never open. Please make it refuse to start until I have picked my own four numbers, and please let me pick them somewhere he is not looking. And add your rescue-USB line to my printed page -- if there is a way to be locked out of my own grandson's computer, I need to know that before it happens, not after.

AGREE and thank you -- 'All done' moving one cell every fortnight is the exact mechanism I could feel but could not name. He does not find that button by looking, he finds it by reaching, and it is the one control he uses when he has had enough. Redrawing its position on a schedule he cannot perceive is the worst possible thing to do to the escape hatch. Same for the band swapping Undo and My Things for two new buttons at T-6 (#55) -- that is a change of the furniture at the exact moment he is already being asked to stop. Pin 'All done' to a fixed cell, and if the band must change, let it ADD rather than replace. And please: whatever the switch is called, make it one switch, not three keys in two files.

AGREE, and your ordering point corrects mine -- I asked for an update button first. You are right that a one-tap pull from ghcr with no signature policy on the device is a worse position than being unpatched, and I would not want that shipped on my say-so. Revised ask: policy.json and the cosign identity pinned on the device FIRST, then the button, then a notification. On the locked parent account plus PasswordAuthentication no: that is not 'awkward for a laptop', that is a device with no recovery path that also contains the only copy of my daughter's drawings. Two consequences worth stating in BUILDING.md today, before anyone installs this on real hardware: (1) never install without a password or key; (2) the child's journal is not backed up anywhere, by anything.

AGREE, and this is my '+10 minutes' button seen from the child's side, so I want to say what I would actually have done. On a Tuesday when we are late I would have opened the gate and given five minutes, thinking I was being kind. If that starts a sitting that is already in 'put your things away', I have just used the one control I was given to break my daughter's afternoon, and she will conclude the machine did it. Two asks. Do not let me give a grant that is too short to be a session -- refuse it in the gate, in words, and tell me what the minimum is. And if the day's budget is genuinely gone, say so at 'Who's here?', before she has told the computer what she is doing afterwards. Better a warm no at the door than a broken promise ninety seconds in.

AGREE, and Priya has named the mechanism better than I did: the grant is the one control the parent is given, and under the current arithmetic using it kindly can BREAK the afternoon. add_minutes is bounded by the daily budget, so a well-meant +5 on a spent day can produce a sitting that is already inside its own ending — and the child will attribute that to the machine, or to her mother, but never to a min() call. Two things I'd add to her asks. Refuse a sub-minimum grant in the gate IN WORDS with the minimum named (adult surface, adult typography — that is what it is for). And when the day's budget is gone, refuse at Who's here, BEFORE 'What's next after?' — otherwise the child has made a plan for after a session she is not going to get.

AGREE, and it changes my own §3 write-up: I had the ending ritual down as the product's strongest feature, and it is — but swapping two band buttons for two different band buttons at T-6 is changing the furniture at the exact moment you are asking a child to stop. In class the visual timetable ADDS the 'tidy up' card to a strip that stays put; you never take a card away to make room. Dan's #57 says the same from home. Concrete ask: at T-6 the offer buttons ADD (band grows or a second row appears), Undo and My Things stay where they were, and the new controls arrive with the reserved highlight so there is an event to notice. And agreed on kidnix-one-more.svg — 'one last little thing' is not a bigger square; for a 5yo it needs to depict the ACTIVITY continuing, or a sand timer with a little left.
